content: The LSTM-Minus method is first proposed in BIBREF6 as a novel way to learn sentence segment embeddings for graph-based dependency parsing, i.e. estimating the most likely dependency tree given an input sentence. For each dependency pair, they divide a sentence into three segments (prefix, infix and suffix), and LSTM-Minus is used to represent each segment. They apply a single LSTM to the whole sentence and use the difference between two hidden states INLINEFORM0 to represent the segment from word INLINEFORM1 to word INLINEFORM2 . This enables their model to learn segment embeddings from information both outside and inside the segments and thus enhancing their model ability to access to sentence-level information. The intuition behind the method is that each hidden vector INLINEFORM3 can capture useful information before and including the word INLINEFORM4 .
